paper_core_claims.claim: The FUSE taxonomy organizes model merging into Foundations, Unification Strategies, Scenarios, and Ecosystem.

The survey distinguishes static parameter unification from structural preservation: averaging and task-vector methods materialize one parameter artifact, whereas MoE-style methods retain experts and add input-conditioned routing.

Shared initialization, architectural compatibility, training-procedure similarity, parameter/representation compatibility, and low interference are presented as mergeability prerequisites, while the authors acknowledge that a complete predictive theory is missing.
The paper synthesizes four principal failure modes: task-level collapse, parameter/sign interference, method-dependent mergeability-prediction failure, and evaluation-masked failure.
The proposed diagnostic sequence checks representation compatibility first, parameter conflict and subspace overlap second, method-specific predictors third, and compositional generalization last.

Evaluation should cover source-task retention, pairwise interference, cross-capability composition, calibration, OOD robustness, computational cost, and safety rather than only aggregate benchmark accuracy.

The manuscript repeatedly describes parts of its examination as systematic, but supplies no literature-search query, database list, date cutoff, inclusion/exclusion criteria, screening flow, duplicate handling, study count, evidence-quality appraisal, or synthesis protocol.
paper_core_claims.anchors: entire manuscript; no review-method section or protocol is present

function_concept_used_by_paper: The survey treats a trained model, task delta, adapter, expert, layer or representation-alignment map as a composable function carrier. Static methods compile these carriers into one checkpoint; structured methods preserve multiple experts and route inputs at runtime; search-based methods treat the merge recipe itself as an optimized meta-function.

representation_or_carrier.static_carriers: aligned full checkpoints, task vectors, layer-wise deltas, masks, Fisher or activation statistics, and scalar or layer-wise coefficients
representation_or_carrier.structured_carriers: separate full-model or LoRA experts, routing keys or gates, and top-k selection state
representation_or_carrier.alignment_carriers: permutation maps, optimal-transport correspondences, feature matches, and representation surgery transforms
representation_or_carrier.search_carriers: candidate recipe encodings, fitness metrics, Pareto objectives, and validation subsets
representation_or_carrier.evaluation_carriers: per-task performance, retention ratios, pairwise interference matrices, calibration, OOD, efficiency, safety and compositional benchmarks
representation_or_carrier.boundary: The taxonomy groups heterogeneous carriers but does not define a common executable type system, schema, compatibility contract, or serialization format.

specification_language: FUSE and Table 5 provide a useful human-readable vocabulary: method category, data requirement, interference handling, shared-initialization requirement, scalability, year, application scenario, and ecosystem. Equations illustrate averaging, task vectors, MoE gates, top-k routing, compatibility prediction, and continual update. The survey does not turn this vocabulary into a machine-readable specification with exact artifact identity, tensor contract, tokenizer/architecture compatibility, coefficient domains, data provenance, effect semantics, failure policy, evaluation thresholds, version rules, or lifecycle transitions.

compiler_or_generator.static: uniform or importance-weighted averaging, task-vector addition/subtraction, sign resolution, sparsification, geometric interpolation, layer-wise or activation-guided selection
compiler_or_generator.structured: preserve or align expert structures and train or derive routing functions
compiler_or_generator.search_based: optimize model choice, layer choice, coefficients, masks, or recipes with validation fitness or multi-objective search
compiler_or_generator.continual: update an existing merged artifact with a new specialist and validation feedback
compiler_or_generator.boundary: These are literature-level method families, not one reference compiler, executable pipeline, or reproduced implementation.

interpreter_or_runtime: A statically unified checkpoint uses its normal model forward pass. Structurally preserved compositions use a gate g_i(x), often softmax or top-k, to select or weight full-model or adapter experts. The survey correctly exposes the memory-versus-interference trade-off, but does not specify runtime authorization, deterministic routing, mixed-version semantics, failure isolation, trace export, latency SLOs, abstention or rollback.
composition_rule: The reviewed families span convex or spherical interpolation, task-vector arithmetic, sign-consensus and sparse delta fusion, Fisher/activation weighting, layer or feature matching, learned dense/top-k expert routing, and evolutionary recipe search. The common boundary is that successful composition depends on carrier compatibility and validation; none of these rules universally preserves behavior, safety or semantic equivalence.
state_or_effect_model: Relevant state includes base and source checkpoint identities, architectures, tokenizers, training lineage, deltas, masks, coefficients, Fisher or activation data, validation samples, router parameters, evaluation traces and output checkpoints. The survey discusses performance, interference, safety, privacy, copyright and compute effects at a narrative level, but defines no shared state schema, effect algebra, access control, atomic promotion, health state, rollback, supersession or retirement protocol.
uncertainty_model: The survey mentions Fisher information, calibration metrics, confidence intervals, significance tests, OOD robustness and predictive compatibility as relevant concepts. It does not quantify uncertainty in its own literature selection or claims, grade evidence quality, report inter-reviewer agreement, distinguish replicated from single-paper findings systematically, or specify calibrated uncertainty for merge decisions. Categorical table labels such as High/Medium scalability and checkmarks lack scoring rules or confidence.

equivalence_notions.boundary: Aligned tensors permit arithmetic but do not prove functional or semantic equivalence.
Low loss along one path is task-, loss-, dataset- and tolerance-dependent and does not guarantee all-capability preservation.
Aggregate retention can mask individual, safety, calibration and compositional failures.
The survey reports these as promising diagnostics, not a universal calibrated compatibility criterion.
Routing probabilities are allocation variables and can collapse or overfit; they are not correctness probabilities.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper names MergeKit, FusionBench, MergeBench, Hugging Face model hubs and many source methods, so it recognizes an ecosystem around artifacts and evaluation. However, the Ecosystem dimension remains mostly tooling and future-direction prose. There is no normative model identity, source hash, license-compatibility record, tokenizer or architecture manifest, merge-recipe schema, evaluation receipt, lineage DAG, approval state, health monitoring, rollback, supersession or retirement model. The paper-specific FUSE taxonomy is not released as a versioned machine-readable artifact.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: This is an arXiv preprint and narrative survey, not a peer-reviewed systematic review or independent empirical study.
Despite repeated 'systematic' wording, no search strategy, databases, date cutoff, inclusion/exclusion, screening, quality appraisal, evidence grading or reproducible review protocol is reported.
The survey contributes no original merge experiment, benchmark reproduction, implementation, dataset or machine-readable taxonomy artifact.
Many claims aggregate heterogeneous studies without consistently distinguishing architecture, scale, task, data access, peer-review status or replication level.
Categorical Table 5 labels such as Data-Free, Interference Handling and Scalability compress substantial protocol differences and have no stated rubric or uncertainty.

The text sometimes turns contingent results into broad statements: shared initialization improves mergeability but does not ensure one loss basin, and overparameterized minima do not generally form a convex subspace supporting arbitrary linear combinations.
Proposition 1 uses approximate stationarity and one smooth loss; it is a loose interpolation bound rather than a capability-preservation guarantee for heterogeneous task losses.
Table 1 attributes 128K context to LLaMA-3 without distinguishing the original Llama 3 release from the later Llama 3.1 context expansion.

The FUSE categories overlap: MoE routing can preserve an ensemble rather than produce a single constituent-cost checkpoint, so it does not fit the introductory definition of merging without qualification.
Ecosystem coverage does not include model-version, provenance, license-compatibility, promotion, monitoring, rollback or retirement governance.
Named evaluation formulas and diagnostic workflows are synthesized recommendations, not validated by this paper across controlled merges.
No uncertainty is attached to literature completeness, evidence quality, taxonomy boundaries or future forecasts.
Safety, privacy, copyright and malicious-contributor risks are acknowledged, but no governed threat model or acceptance standard is specified.
The survey correctly reports that method-dependent mergeability and evaluation-masked failures prevent a single static metric or aggregate benchmark from certifying a merge.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that model merging preserves source capabilities, safety, privacy, calibration or semantic equivalence.
It does not establish that any listed method is universally best, production-ready, or independently reproduced by the survey authors.
It does not provide a systematic-review completeness guarantee or quantitative meta-analysis.
It does not provide a governed VersionedRegistry, executable Function OS, or validation of the point architecture as a whole.

GAP-016.reason: The survey maps many compiler families, yet contributes and validates no executable generator of its own.

GAP-017.reason: Mode connectivity, permutation symmetry, representation divergence, subspace overlap and retention expose multiple non-equivalent compatibility notions and their boundaries.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: The survey maps static composition, learned routing, activation guidance, structural preservation and search trade-offs directly.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Tools and model hubs are named, but artifact identity, provenance, compatibility, health, rollback, supersession and retirement governance are absent.

confirmed_projection: The FUSE taxonomy and full survey provide direct secondary-source support for a broad Representation-Interpreter-Validator-ComposerRouter map: model-merging carriers, static and routed composition families, mergeability notions, failure modes, evaluation dimensions and tool categories are all explicit. Compiler implementation, primary empirical validation, evidence-grade uncertainty and VersionedRegistry lifecycle remain partial.
source_specific_reasoning: This source is valuable as a design-space map, not as primary proof. Its strongest contribution is the explicit separation of foundations, unification mechanisms, scenarios and ecosystem, plus the four-failure-mode diagnostic sequence and multi-dimensional validation checklist. Overall support remains PARTIAL because the authors do not execute any method or benchmark and do not report a reproducible review protocol despite systematic-review language. Consequently, cited results must be accepted or rejected at their primary sources, and the survey cannot independently confirm effectiveness, safety, privacy, completeness or production lifecycle.
projection_boundary: All GAP and Function OS impacts above are 121CX architectural projections from arXiv v2. This card treats cited empirical and theoretical findings as secondary-source summaries unless separately reviewed at their primary sources. It is not a meta-analysis, benchmark reproduction, proof, safety review, registry certification, or final truth freeze.
